note: The document catalogue. Each requirement is a document or action the pack can produce. 'when' is checked against the derivation result (or, with 'per', against each node of that type). 'status' rules are checked top to bottom; the first match sets the status, otherwise it is to do. 'cause' says which lever or edge produced it: a list of screening answers, or a node type and condition. 'rail: false' means it is always in the pack but not shown as a to-do in the rail.

requirements.title: One-page summary
requirements.filled_from: story, diagram, verdict, cheapest change, cost of safer version
requirements.meaning: A single page that says whether you can do this and what it would take.

requirements.title: Action plan
requirements.filled_from: every open requirement as a numbered step with owner and effort
requirements.meaning: The list of things to do, in order, with who and how long.

requirements.title: DPIA screening record
requirements.filled_from: A1 to A17 with because, outcome, rationale, cheapest change
requirements.meaning: The form that shows whether a full assessment is needed and why.

requirements.title: Data flow diagram
requirements.meaning: The picture of where data goes.

requirements.title: Article 28 DPA
requirements.filled_from: role, Article 28 checklist, sub-processors, hosting, retention, status
requirements.meaning: Proof that this company is contractually bound to look after the data.

requirements.title: Sub-processor check
requirements.meaning: Confirms the company behind the company is allowed.

requirements.title: Supplier question sheet
requirements.filled_from: products.json supplier_questions, addressed to the company
requirements.meaning: The questions to send a supplier we don't have an agreement with yet.

requirements.title: Record of processing entry
requirements.filled_from: purpose, data categories, subjects, recipients, retention, lawful basis
requirements.meaning: The line in the organisation's register that says this processing exists.

requirements.title: Retention note
requirements.when: highest_tier >= 1 && (any(company, keeps_data) || any(company, retention in ['', 'unknown', null]))
requirements.filled_from: what is kept, where, how long, who deletes
requirements.meaning: A written statement of how long the data is kept and who deletes it.

requirements.title: Tier decision note
requirements.meaning: Why this data is the tier it is and what that allows.

requirements.title: Lawful basis statement
requirements.filled_from: basis per data category; LIA stub if legitimate interests
requirements.meaning: The legal reason you are allowed to use this data.

requirements.title: Privacy notice paragraph

cause.text: named data goes into AI, so people must be told

requirements.meaning: The sentence that tells people this is happening to their data.

requirements.title: Human review procedure
requirements.filled_from: who checks, how to challenge, how a decision is changed
requirements.meaning: How a person can question and change what the system produced.

requirements.title: Transfer mechanism note
requirements.left_for_person: confirm the mechanism is in place
requirements.meaning: How data is allowed to leave the UK.

requirements.title: Children's code check
requirements.filled_from: the age appropriate design code questions
requirements.meaning: Extra questions because under 18s use it directly.

requirements.title: Full DPIA
requirements.filled_from: steps 1, 2 and 4 from the parts above; starter risk list from triggers
requirements.left_for_person: consultation, risk scoring, measures adopted, sign-off
requirements.meaning: The full assessment, because the screening found high risk.

requirements.title: Data sharing agreement outline
requirements.meaning: What two organisations agree when they both control the data.
